sentence: This project builds computational tools that measure and interpret the DNA changes made by CRISPR genome editing.
This project builds a patient-specific model of breast cancer metastasis and studies how cancer and the immune system interact as it spreads.
This project finds, sequences and describes complex structural variation in the human genome that has been hard to assemble.
This project tries to find out how microbes and host pathways let Clostridioides difficile live silently in older people and people eating high-sugar diets.
This project studies how one gene maintains genome architecture during aging.
This project uses focused ultrasound to help cellular immunotherapy reach and stay in high-risk medulloblastoma, a brain tumor.
This project improves ultrasound tomography so it can image breast tissue in finer detail for cancer screening without compression or ionizing radiation.
This project develops ways to insert antibody genes into B cells with precision genome editing, as a possible treatment for HIV infection.
This project builds a sequencing platform that tells one kind of uridine modification from others in human RNA from lung adenocarcinoma.
This project builds microscopy tools that use scattered light to image molecules and cells without labels.
This project studies how one allele causes early vascular problems that come before amyloid and tau changes in Alzheimer's disease.
This project studies what causes keloids, a wound healing disorder.
This project builds a light-sheet fluorescence microscope that can image many things, from single cells to cleared tissues.
This project studies whether blocking Renalase, a target gene, can protect beta cells from stress and autoimmune attacks in early type 1 diabetes.
This project studies how differences within tumors of the bile ducts affect how the cancer grows, spreads and resists treatment.
This project studies how neurocognitive and patient-reported outcomes change in the year after chimeric antigen receptor T-cell therapy for lymphoma.
This project builds a way to use lipid nanoparticles to deliver genome editing reagents into nematodes without microinjection.
This project studies how nicotinic acetylcholine receptors in a brain pathway affect ethanol consumption and negative mood after stopping alcohol.
This project tests two ways to treat hereditary fructose intolerance in mice, by turning down fructose processing or repairing mutations with gene editing.
This project builds an AI model that predicts how cells change over time and space, including cell fate and disease progression.
